name: aadhar-sh
description: aadhar.sh - deploy-time transform only (authoring stays buildless; see build.mjs)
comment:workspaces: bun DOES read npm's `workspaces` field, which pnpm did not — so the package list moved here out of pnpm-workspace.yaml and that file is gone. Everything else it carried had to split three ways: `overrides` and `trustedDependencies` are package.json fields below, and the release-age policy is bunfig.toml. Read bunfig.toml before changing either.
comment:exec: `pnpm exec X` became bare `X` in these scripts, NOT `bunx X`. Measured 2026-08-16 on 1.4.0-canary.1: `bun x wrangler --version` in an empty directory with no local install resolved, downloaded and ran 4.123.0 from the registry. That is the npx hole gotcha 29 closed, wearing bun's name. Bare works because bun puts node_modules/.bin on PATH for a script it runs. Code that spawns wrangler OUTSIDE a script (deploy-promote.mjs, perf-budget.mjs) cannot assume that PATH and uses `bun x --no-install wrangler`, where --no-install is an explicit refusal to fetch (probed: errors on a missing package rather than downloading it).
comment:trustedDependencies: bun's spelling of pnpm's `allowBuilds`. Same three packages, same measured reasoning: each ships its platform binary through optionalDependencies and passes its probe with the postinstall blocked, so these are approved to match what the packages intend rather than because anything breaks without them. Semantic note: defining this key REPLACES bun's built-in default allowlist, so the tree stays default-deny exactly as it was.
comment:overrides: GHSA / dependabot #12: nanoid before 3.3.17 spins forever in customAlphabet and customRandom when size is 0. Dev-only, one position, vitest -> vite -> postcss -> nanoid; nothing a Worker serves touches it. FIDELITY LOSS WORTH KNOWING: pnpm wrote this as the SELECTOR `nanoid@<3.3.17: ^3.3.17`, which matches only the versions the advisory names and therefore EXPIRES ON ITS OWN the day postcss raises its floor past 3.3.17. bun overrides map a bare name to a version and support no selector, so this pin is unconditional and will silently hold every future nanoid resolution at a 2026 patch release. Re-check by hand when postcss moves; nothing here will tell you.

scripts.dev:remote: bun tools/compose-dev.mjs && bun tools/gen-remote-config.mjs wrangler.dev.jsonc && wrangler dev -c .wrangler.remote.jsonc
scripts.photos:env: uv venv tools/photos/.venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing && uv pip install --python tools/photos/.venv/bin/python -r tools/photos/requirements.txt

comment:undici: undici arrives only through miniflare, which pins it EXACTLY, so npm cannot move it and dependabot cannot either. An `overrides` block forced 7.29.0 from 2026-08-05 until this commit, for five advisories in the 7.28.0 pin. Both miniflare consumers now ask for 7.29.0 themselves, so the override is gone. The floors are what replace it: `wrangler >= 4.120.0` and `cal`'s `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers >= 0.20.3` are the two versions whose miniflare (5.20260801.1-alpha) carries the fixed pin. Dropping EITHER floor puts 7.28.0 back at the hoisted position, silently, because npm hoists whichever exact pin it resolves first and the vulnerable one wins that race.
comment:node-pinned-scripts: THREE scripts still say `node` on purpose, and the reason is measured rather than cautious. `routes:check` boots this repo Worker in-process through wrangler createTestHarness(); under bun 1.4.0-canary.1 that HANGS with no output and no error (killed at 13 minutes, 5 workerd children idle at 0.7% CPU), while the identical call under node v26.7.0 sweeps 136 routes and exits 0. createTestHarness() itself constructs fine under bun — the hang is at listen(), which is where workerd is actually spawned and wrangler build.command runs. wrangler, miniflare and workerd are the deploy path AND the route oracle, and they are node-pinned; this is that pin surfacing rather than a bun defect we can route around. Re-test with `bun tools/check-routes-harness.mjs` when bun 1.4 ships stable, and if it passes, delete this comment and the word node.
